- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; increase forecast moderately, especially if recent price is falling.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp upward moves (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days) — cap forecast at 10–15% above recent peak if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., +0.67 → -0.33), model often fails to adjust — apply mean reversion bias: forecast = prior 5-day average + 0.5×(true - prior 5-day avg) if sentiment shifts.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (e.g., first 5–7 days) — dampen initial forecast by 2–5% if sentiment is weak or mixed.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥ 0.8) and price is rising, model may overfit trend — reduce forecast by 3–5% if price is above 70.00 and sentiment > 0.8.
- If sentiment is low (≤ 0.3) and price is falling, model often undercorrects — increase forecast by 2–4% if price is below 65.00 and sentiment < 0.3.
